newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast crudes continue to feel LATAM pressures.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast crudes continue to feel LATAM pressures.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude markets were inactive midday Monday, with all types of South American grades undercutting fundamentals for local prices, traders said.
Astra continued to offer South Blend cargo (29 API, 0.8 sulphur) to West Coast (PADD 5) refiners at a price rumored to be 60 to 80 cents a gallon under ANS.

Two major producers and one refinery offered large parcels of Line 63 light, a blended crude similar to ANS. They asked for 70 cents over Buena Vista grade crude, 30 cents under the last reported deal.
Two were sized at 4,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) for May, and a third for 5,000 bpd.
On a notional basis, Line 63 was talked $2.37/2.27 under May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI). The grade rarely trades off WTI.
BP Oil, the dominant seller of ANS, last offered at 95 cents below May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) but refiners said the price remained out-of-synch with supply and demand.
In heavy crude markets, all California lowered prices for Point Arguello offshore crude by 0.50 cents a barrel as of April 17.
With more Venezuelan and Mexican heavy grades moving into the U.S. Gulf, shipments of Point Arguello east have been discounted into the West Coast.
West Coast benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) last traded a week ago at $1.32 below West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI), which compared with a week earlier at $1.05 below.
Outright ANS prices rose 50 cents a barrel, in line with a technical rise in West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude Monday.
